_comment: Mutations for the REVERSE direction of the .dockerignore contract: a
pattern may not sweep a TRACKED file out of the ROOT build context.
THE GAP THESE MUTANTS CLOSE
tests/test_dockerignore_covers_gitignore.py only checks the FORWARD
direction ('every .gitignore pattern has a covering .dockerignore
pattern'). The reverse direction -- 'does a .dockerignore pattern
exclude a file git TRACKS' -- was measured (zero regression today: the
273 excluded tracked files are all pre-existing) but NOTHING PINNED it,
so a future pattern could silently drop a tracked file out of the
image and make the running service differ from the published source
archive. tests/test_dockerignore_tracked_files.py pins it: the excluded
set must be EXACTLY the documented allowlist -- neither more nor fewer.
M1 (product) a new pattern sweeps a tracked file out of the root
context. AGENTS.md is tracked and is currently IN the image; the
mutant excludes it. A subset-only comparison would MISS this, the
exact-set comparison kills it.
M2 (product) the '!.env.example' negation is gone, so the tracked
.env.example falls back to the '.env.*' rule and leaves the
image. This is the last-rule-wins / negation semantics at work.
M3 (product) the 'tests/' rule is gone: the allowlist entry goes stale
and the excluded set shrinks, which is the 'silently shrunken
allowlist' half of the rule.
M4 (test) the matcher loses directory-prefix semantics: 'a/b' stops
covering 'a/b/c.txt'. The controls AND the rule test catch it.
M5 (test) the matcher stops honouring the '!' negation.
M6 (test) the allowlist is loosened to 'any tracked file under a
prefix' -- a broad 'frontend/' entry -- without an exact-set
check. The exact-set test kills it.
M7 (test) the allowlist silently SHRINKS: the 'docs/' entry is gone.
The exact-set test kills it.
M8 (test) the EXACTNESS COMPARISON is weakened to a subset check,
'excluded <= allowlist': a new exclusion would pass unnoticed.
M9 (test) the matcher applies the FIRST matching rule instead of the
LAST one, so a later negation can no longer re-include a file.
M10 (test) the exactness comparison is weakened to the OTHER subset
check, 'allowlist <= excluded': a shrunken allowlist would pass.
M11 (test) the WSL path translation is gone, so the worktree's git dir
cannot be resolved under WSL and the tracked-file list comes back
empty. The rule tests must then FAIL (never skip) -- the tracked list
is resolved through the worktree's git dir, so the rule tests cannot
skip in the harness.
M12 (test) the loud failure is silent again: the tracked list becomes
None instead of raising. The new 'obtainable' test must FAIL.
M8 AND M10 ARE KILLED, NOT EXPECTED SURVIVORS. A verdict computed
inline in a test cannot be weakened-detected: while the product is
correct a subset check and an exact check agree, so no test could tell
them apart. The comparison therefore lives in a named CALLABLE,
allowlist_matches_exactly(), and is called DIRECTLY with deliberately
inconsistent SYNTHETIC pairs (equal, strict subset, superset, disjoint,
empty/non-empty). The direct test depends on no repository data, so the
product state cannot satisfy it -- only a genuinely exact comparison
can. M8 and M10 therefore go red in the same way as every other mutant.
THE TRACKED LIST IS RESOLVED THROUGH THE WORKTREE'S GIT DIR
This checkout is a LINKED worktree: its .git is a FILE holding a Windows
drive path ('gitdir: C:/dev/DepthSight/.git/worktrees/...'). Under WSL --
where the mutation harness runs pytest -- git resolves that path RELATIVE
to the current directory and fails with rc=128, so the tracked-file list
used to come back None, the four rule tests SKIPPED, pytest exited 0 and
M1, M2, M3, M6 and M7 were recorded as SURVIVORS. The product WAS defended
and the GUARD was SILENT. tracked_files() therefore asks git for the
worktree's git dir EXPLICITLY (translating a Windows drive path to the
WSL mount point as well), and require_tracked_files() FAILS LOUDLY when
the list cannot be resolved in a checkout -- never a skip. M11 and M12 pin
those two halves.
Every needle is a SINGLE contiguous string and each occurs EXACTLY ONCE
in its target file (counted against the file's bytes before use). The
harness tries the CRLF form first and the LF form second, because this
worktree is mixed: .dockerignore is CRLF here, and the new test file is
LF (like its sibling tests/test_dockerignore_covers_gitignore.py).
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/dockerignore_tracked_files.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: M1: a new .dockerignore pattern sweeps the tracked AGENTS.md out of the root build context
M2: the '!.env.example' negation is gone, so the tracked .env.example leaves the image
M3: the 'tests/' rule is gone, so the allowlist entry goes stale and the excluded set shrinks
M4: the matcher loses directory-prefix semantics, so 'a/b' stops covering 'a/b/c.txt'
M5: the matcher stops honouring the '!' negation
M6: the allowlist is loosened to 'any tracked file under a prefix' with no exact-set check
mutations.needle:
("dir", "tests/",
     "the runtime services never import the test suite (alembic needs "
     "alembic/ + alembic.ini); the AGPL offer publishes it in the archive"),
mutations.replace:
("dir", "tests/",
     "the runtime services never import the test suite (alembic needs "
     "alembic/ + alembic.ini); the AGPL offer publishes it in the archive"),
    ("dir", "frontend/",
     "MUTANT: any tracked file under a prefix"),

mutations.label: M7: the allowlist silently shrinks -- the 'docs/' entry is gone
mutations.needle:
("dir", "docs/",
     "documentation is not needed at runtime; the AGPL offer publishes it in "
     "the source archive"),

mutations.label: M8: the exactness comparison is weakened to a subset check ('excluded <= allowlist'), so a new exclusion would pass unnoticed
M9: the matcher applies the FIRST matching rule instead of the LAST, so a later negation cannot re-include a file
M10: the exactness comparison is weakened to the OTHER subset check ('allowlist <= excluded'), so a shrunken allowlist would pass unnoticed
M11: the WSL path translation is gone, so the worktree's git dir cannot be resolved under WSL and the tracked-file list is empty
M12: the loud failure is silent again -- the tracked list becomes None instead of raising, so a broken resolution would not fail
mutations.needle:
raise AssertionError(
            "git ls-files failed in this checkout: the tracked-file list is "
            "unavailable, so the .dockerignore tracked-file rules would be "
            "vacuous. See tests/test_gitignore_ignores_env_copies.py for the "
            "same guard."
        )
